A day for each feast

Losar (Tibetan New Year)

Losar Celebration: Tibetan New Year at Home

Celebrate Losar by honoring Tibetan traditions with meaningful rituals, visits, and special foods that usher in good fortune for the new year.

  1. Morning

    Clean and Replace Prayer Flags

    Begin the day by replacing old prayer flag streamers with fresh ones to invite blessings and positive energy into your home.

  2. Mid-Morning

    Visit a Local Monastery or Watch Cham Dances

    If possible, visit a nearby monastery to observe or participate in the traditional cham dances, which symbolize the triumph of good over evil.

  3. Noon

    Exchange Khata Scarves with Auspicious Wishes

    Gather family members to exchange khata scarves while reciting blessings and wishes for health, happiness, and prosperity in the coming year.

  4. Early Afternoon

    Prepare Guthuk Noodle Soup with Symbolic Dumplings

    Cook guthuk noodle soup featuring nine special dumplings, each containing symbolic ingredients that represent traits or fortunes for the new year.

    Recipes: Guthuk Noodle Soup

  5. Mid-Afternoon

    Make and Enjoy Khapse Pastries

    Bake or serve deep-fried khapse pastries, a festive treat traditionally enjoyed during Losar to celebrate the season.

    Recipes: Khapse Pastries

  6. Late Afternoon

    Serve Dried Yak Cheese and Butter Tea

    Share dried yak cheese and freshly brewed butter tea with family and neighbors to foster community bonds and warm spirits.

    Recipes: Dried Yak Cheese · Traditional Tibetan Butter Tea

  7. Evening

    Reflect and Share Stories

    Conclude the day by gathering together to share stories, reflect on the past year, and express hopes for the year ahead.

End your Losar day feeling connected, hopeful, and ready to embrace the new year with joy and tradition.
